questions.modelAnswer: Photosynthesis lets plants build their own carbohydrates from simple raw materials, powered by light energy.

questions.stem: Name the sugar that photosynthesis produces.
Explain why light energy is not classed as a raw material.
questions.modelAnswer: Because raw materials are substances converted into the products, and light is not a substance; it is the energy source that drives the conversion of carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.

questions.stem: A plant in darkness is fed glucose solution through its roots. Predict whether it still needs photosynthesis that night.
questions.modelAnswer: For respiration it does not — the supplied glucose can fuel energy release immediately; but it still needs light-driven photosynthesis to build its starch reserves, cellulose and other molecules once the external glucose runs out.

questions.stem: Write the word equation for photosynthesis.
questions.modelAnswer: Carbon dioxide plus water, using light energy, produce glucose plus oxygen.

questions.stem: State the balanced symbol equation for photosynthesis.
questions.modelAnswer: Six CO2 plus six H2O produce C6H12O6 plus six O2.

questions.stem: Explain why learning one equation gives you the other for free.
questions.modelAnswer: Because photosynthesis and aerobic respiration run in exact reverse: what photosynthesis takes in, respiration gives out, and vice versa, so mastering one balanced equation hands you the other by reading it backwards.

questions.stem: A student writes 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 4O2. Diagnose and correct the error.
questions.modelAnswer: The oxygen atoms do not balance: the left side holds eighteen, and the student's version holds only sixteen; the glucose contains six, so twelve oxygen atoms must remain as products, giving six O2 molecules on the right.
